recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Predictive Programming, the Queen, and 1836", "body": "Gabe argued that the film seeded imagery before the Queen's death, pointing to her birth as Elizabeth of York, her death in Scotland and the Virgo timing, which he read in the opening gap scene as Saturn combing the hair of Virgo. He wondered whether hiding royal dates could be mystical. Late in the show Gabe marked the incursion line as the exact halfway point of the film, counted 18 minutes and 36 seconds to a matching echo in the water tunnel, and tied the year 1836 to the Texas Revolution, the Queen's birthday and the Ancient Order of Hibernians. He promised more next time."}, {"title": "The Dark Hold as Black's Law Dictionary", "body": "Chance argued that the Mordo and Strange conversation worked as a metaphor for the legal system. He proposed that demons and monsters stood in for the legal straw man, that the Dark Hold was Black's Law Dictionary, and that the Book of Vishanti was the Bible, the white book set against the black book. He read dreamwalking as acting in public through a fictional double while hidden in the private. One host compared dreamwalkers to agents provocateurs, and Chance later read Strange's courtroom trial as a charge laid against the straw man rather than the living man."}, {"title": "Wordplay and Lumashi Decoding", "body": "The hosts played constantly with etymology, anagram and pun. One host noted that Amor es amor on America's jacket read as Roma backwards and set it beside the two Roms, the Holy See and Vatican City. Another linked the Greek word storge to Strange. A viewer comment read aloud held that the Gaelic word for secret is run, which fit the secret imagery before Wanda took over a mind. One host credited a viewer for the Braille sign encoding pi, then tied Braille to Libra. They called this approach Lumashi, or constellation writing."}, {"title": "The Council as the Bill of Rights", "body": "Gabe laid out a theory that the Illuminati council members embodied constitutional amendments, encoded in their powers, dialogue and deaths. He matched Black Bolt to the First Amendment, Reed Richards to the Second, Professor Xavier to the Third, Maria Rambeau to the Fourth, Mordo to the Sixth and the film's antagonist to Hecate and the Eighth, with Strange himself as the empty seventh seat. After hearing a show on sacred architecture, Gabe also matched the figures to the Apotheosis of George Washington in the Capitol rotunda. The group agreed to continue in a part three."}, {"title": "Wondagor, Chthon, and the Fear of Winter", "body": "Chance read Mount Wondagor as the axis mundi, a polar throne for Sophia. One host tied the Chthon reference to underworld and winter powers, and another argued that the germ fear in the Illuminati cells echoed the oldest human fear of night and winter. Gordy read Strange's third eye as a symbol of godlike paranormal power rather than integration, and argued that the multiverses were dreams. The hosts also previewed the later duel as a fight over unspoken trauma between two versions of Strange."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The InnerVersal mystics of Marvel return to integrate the shadow of the Dark Mother Goddess & the Man of Light, with an incredibly deep analysis of Dr. Strange and the Multiverse of Madness. Rife with Gnostic Christian allegory and a psychologically shattered-mirror perspective on the All-Mother, this film may just be the wildest thing we've covered yet.
